summary: Unseen mini-wave causing slot-locks and autoscaler suppression in dedicated pool
description:
Issue summary: Verdant Health reports recurring brief capacity dropouts in their dedicated GPU cluster over a 6-hour window. Impact: sustained p50 throughput drop ~20% and p99 latency spike to ~2.5x baseline for multi-tenant batched routes. Users observed brief request errors (HTTP 503) and increased fallback to hosted variants.

Observed pattern: the degradation appears as short (30-90s) mini-waves of slot locks where a subset of GPU slots become unassignable, autoscaler reduces target concurrently (suppression), and throughput does not recover until ~2 minutes after wave subsides. The pattern repeats every ~7-15 minutes during the window.

Why this ticket is unique: behavior isn't typical noisy-tenant saturation (no single tenant dominates) and it's not classic nvlink/thermal throttling. Hypothesis space includes transient prefetch contention, heartbeat suppression from connection pool eviction, or a thin background IO job overlapping with prefetch windows.

steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use dedicated pool with Verdant's traffic pattern: many short streams (~200-500ms) and occasional long streaming requests
2) Route to a batched route pinned to open-llama-13b on dedicated pool in us-east-1
3) Run a synthetic miniwave generator that sends small bursts spaced ~8 minutes apart to simulate observed cadence
4) Observe allocator logs and autoscaler target changes during bursts; look for slot_unassignable and allocator_rebalance events

investigation_notes: Initial observation: waves align with short background snapshot writes from snapshotter service (start ~200-500ms before slot_unassignable events)
Probe 1: throttling snapshotter during a controlled window in staging reduced frequency of slot locks, but did not eliminate them entirely
Probe 2: increased prefetch lease timeout in a canary reduced eviction_spike counts by ~60% and improved immediate recovery to baseline throughput

Hypothesis A: small concurrent IO bursts (snapshotter + prefetch eviction) cause brief NVME or host IO queue saturation, delaying allocator heartbeats and causing transient slot state 'locked' that autoscaler interprets as capacity shortfall and suppresses scale-up
Hypothesis B: connection pool eviction resulting in heartbeat jitter to allocator; observed small spikes in heartbeat latency (50-120ms) at wave start
Finding: not a single noisy tenant; traces show multiple tenants contribute small prefetched caches simultaneously — aggregate effect resembles a noisy-neighbor but distributed

Next action: reproduce with controlled snapshotter and prefetcher settings on a dedicated test pool; instrument kernel-level NVME queue depths and allocator heartbeat metrics; propose a transient autoscaler guard to ignore single-short-slot-unassignable bursts under X seconds

Verdant-Eng 2026-03-10: Provided route IDs batched-v1, tenant tags, and a 6-hour pcap. Confirmed traffic pattern: short chat messages, occasional long streaming upload.
Evan Li 2026-03-10: Found allocator WARNs. Correlated timestamp with snapshotter writes. Running controlled test to disable snapshotter in a canary.
Aisha Khan 2026-03-11: Notified customer about planned canary and ETA for guarded autoscaler tweak. SLA 4-hour first response met.

Evan Li 2026-03-11: Canary results: with snapshotter disabled, waves reduced frequency by ~75%. Prefetch timeouts still caused isolated slot locks. Drafting PR to introduce autoscaler suppression guard: ignore slot_unassignable events shorter than 60s when prefetch_eviction spikes detected. See PR github.com/redwood/repro/PR-4821
Verdant-Eng 2026-03-12: Confirmed temporary mitigation improved their p50 throughput by ~15% during peak window. Awaiting permanent fix and rollout schedule.
resolution: Mitigation in progress. Short-term: scheduled a staged change to autoscaler to add a 60s grace window before shrinking target when the event is a slot_unassignable spike correlated with prefetcher eviction metric. Also scheduled snapshotter IO smoothing for Verdant's dedicated pool (throttle writes and stagger checkpoints). Long-term: instrument NVME queue depth metrics and add allocator heartbeat redundancy. Customer has seen improvement in canary; monitoring for 48 hours before closing. Rollout PR: github.com/redwood/repro/PR-4821
